top.description: Oregon football’s season hasn’t worked out the way it expected. But the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) were ranked in the first College Football Playoff rankings. The No. 23 Ducks are coming off a confidence-boosting win over Northwestern, heading on the road to face No. 12 Ohio State (6-2, 4-1) this Saturday. That matchup originally included the preseason Nos. 1 and 2 teams in the AP poll. But in this chaotic college football season, the Buckeyes are reeling after a road loss to No. 20 USC. Other Big Ten teams in this week’s CFP rankings include No. 19 Iowa, No. 8 UCLA and No. 4 Indiana. top.title: Ravens’ Jesse Minter doesn’t hold back on ‘unacceptable’ play after latest blowout loss
top.description: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Ravens’ Jesse Minter doesn’t hold back on ‘unacceptable’ play after latest blowout loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens suffered a blowout 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football, extending their losing skid to four straight games. The Ravens started undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano amid their quarterback injury crisis, and he was unable to make much of an impact in the game after the Ravens went down big. While Ravens head coach Jesse Minter acknowledged the team was in a tough spot with Fagnano starting, he was not pleased with their second-half showing . “In the second half, we just got in our own way. We’re turning the ball over a couple times in a row. The defense was out there, it felt like the whole half. I thought they battled and fought, and did a decent job in the second half. But obviously, the results are not acceptable for us and what we’re after,” Minter said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After a relatively clean first half, Fagnano immediately threw an interception in the first drive of the second half, which led to a Jaguars field goal. The Ravens then committed back-to-back turnovers with another pick and a fumble to start the fourth quarter, which allowed the Jags to blow the game wide open. These second-half collapses are becoming a common occurrence for the Ravens. Their current four-game losing streak started with back-to-back meltdowns against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals with Tyler Huntley at quarterback. While the absence of Lamar Jackson amid this skid has been huge, Minter has much work to do in terms of keeping his team playing to a high standard for the entire game. top.title: Ilia Topuria Opens Up on Psychological Impact of Justin Gaethje Loss in First Interview Since UFC Freedom 250
top.description: Ilia Topuria’s UFC return is gaining momentum with each passing day. A couple of days ago, the former two-division champion visited his native Georgia, giving fans a glimpse of his recovery. More recently, he stopped by the iconic Didgori Battle Memorial on Mount Didgori, a site that symbolizes Georgian resilience and victory. Amid all this, Dana White also provided an important update on Topuria’s status , confirming that the Spaniard is expected to be ready to return in the first quarter of 2027. With contenders like Paddy Pimblett and Arman Tsarukyan , along with reigning champion Justin Gaethje, in the mix, it will be interesting to see what’s next for “El Matador.” “He’ll be back in ’27. We’re working on that too.” @DanaWhite confirms Ilia Topuria’s return to #UFC will happen next year. https://t.co/tbRDbrnMo4 — Jim Rome (@jimrome) November 4, 2026 ALSO READ: Dana White Gives Green Light to Alexander Volkanovski vs. Justin Gaethje Lightweight Title Fight, Reveals Potential Roadblock However, Topuria recently sat down for his first exclusive interview since his loss to Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 in June 2026. In a preview clip released by ABC Diario on Thursday, fans got a glimpse of the Spaniard’s mindset after suffering the first defeat of his professional career and falling to 17-1. He said, “I’ve been in the worst situation a fighter can possibly be in. I’ve experienced the worst day of my career. What’s worse than that? Dying?” Topuria also opened up about the psychological impact of the defeat, admitting that he had spent months questioning what went wrong. “Was something off is a question I’ve had to face over the last five or six months, but one thing is clear: you either win, or you lose; and I lost. If I wake up in the morning and look in the mirror and it was like, ‘No, no, no, no, no, this is not me.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by ABC (@abc_diario) This isn’t the first time Topuria has opened up about the loss. Back in September, he took to social media to reflect on the devastating defeat in a short video essay addressed to his son, Hugo. He offered an even deeper look into his experience following his first MMA defeat. The former double champion published a lengthy nine-part piece titled “This Is Me” on his website, taking readers through his entire journey in the sport. Topuria candidly revealed that he struggled to recognize his own face when he looked in the mirror the morning after his fight with Gaethje. He also disclosed that he suffered fractures to both orbital bones, a broken septum, and a broken foot during their brutal back-and-forth encounter. Of course, Topuria was eventually forced to retire on his stool at the end of the fourth round against Gaethje at the White House. Now, with his return potentially just months away, the big question is whether “El Matador” can rediscover the confidence that made him one of the UFC’s most feared fighters.

top.title: REPORT: Warsofsky’s Job Safe for Now
top.description: San Jose Sharks head coach Ryan Warsofsky isn’t on the hot seat yet. That’s what Pierre LeBrun reported on TSN’s Insider Trading on Thursday. “The Sharks are near the bottom in goals for. They’re near the bottom in goals against. It’s ugly. The team’s struggles have led to speculation about Ryan Warsofsky,” LeBrun said. “My understanding is that Sharks GM Mike Grier is not contemplating a coaching change at this stage.” The San Jose Sharks, after a 6-4-1 start, have slumped, losing five of their last six. They got stomped 7-2 at the Los Angeles Kings on Wednesday, leading to a players-only meeting. “It’s not on the coaches right now,” Kiefer Sherwood said afterwards. Warsofsky, going into the last year of his contract, signed a multi-year extension before the season. Warsofsky and his coaching staff, spearheaded by an MVP-caliber Macklin Celebrini campaign, had led a 34-point improvement in the standings last year. Grier followed that up in the off-season by committing over $100 million to veterans Mason Marchment , Darnell Nurse , Jacob Trouba, and Michael Kesselring, raising expectations for a San Jose playoff berth, which would be their first since 2019. But dragged down by mostly poor 5-on-5 play, along with injuries to glue center Alex Wennberg and top winger Igor Chernyshov, the Sharks have sputtered recently. It looks like Warsofsky will get some time to turn the San Jose Sharks around. But for how long? Related Headlines Sharks Insight: Does San Jose Need Different Voice Besides Warsofsky? top.title: ‘Bro, let me tell you’: Ayo Dosunmu shares what has shocked him about LaMelo Ball
top.description: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images LaMelo Ball is one of the most fun players to watch in the NBA. The Minnesota Timberwolves superstar has had an incredible start to the season, and some of the shots he has pulled off have been incredible to see. Ball’s teammate, Ayo Dosunmu, has now shed some light on what the 25-year-old is actually like behind the scenes. Ayo Dosunmu says he has never seen anyone like LaMelo Ball One of the first things people usually say about Ball is that he is ‘too chill’. Dosunmu has heard that several times, but he wants to tell everyone that his Minnesota Timberwolves teammate is actually very serious about the game. Despite being a superstar and worth an absolute fortune, Ball apparently asks more questions in practice than anyone else to improve his game. That seems to have surprised Dosunmu, as he had never seen anyone do the above. Speaking about people’s perception that “LaMelo is too chill,” he wrote in The Players’ Tribune : “Bro, let me tell you something about LaMelo. “He’s more curious about the game of basketball than anybody I’ve ever seen at his level. How many guys who are worth $300 million are still asking questions every day in practice? “He’s worth $300 million, and he’s trying to learn and get better every day.” That mentality is exactly what separates a good player from a great one, and it is no surprise to see Ball perform so well since the start of the season. With Anthony Edwards out injured, the Timberwolves need Ball to become more of a leader and deliver. So far, he has been doing that. top.title: ‘Wanting to win’: Justin Jefferson breaks silence on frustration with Vikings offense
top.description: Eric Hartline-USA TODAY Sports The Minnesota Vikings suffered their first loss of the season on Sunday, falling 19-15 to the Detroit Lions. And star wide receiver Justin Jefferson couldn’t hide his frustration, as the Vikings’ passing game struggled once again. Now, Jefferson has finally addressed what was bothering him. Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Jefferson said his frustration came from “wanting to win,” and warned that the Vikings are “wasting” the talent they have on offense if they don’t start executing. Jefferson’s Frustration Jefferson made one of the most impressive catches of the season on Sunday, tipping a pass to himself for a 1-yard touchdown. But he finished with just five catches for 33 yards, as quarterback Kyler Murray missed him on several throws, including an interception right before halftime. Jefferson, a two-time winner of the Korey Stringer Good Guy Award for his cooperation with local media, didn’t speak to reporters after the game. But both Murray and head coach Kevin O’Connell acknowledged that he was frustrated. “Obviously he’s frustrated, and that’s understandable. He is who he is, and he has every right to the way he feels when he doesn’t get the ball. That’s on us to find a way to get him the ball,” Murray said, via ESPN’s Kevin Seifert . “These guys want to win. I don’t fault the frustration or the competitiveness in any way, shape or form,” O’Connell added. Despite the Vikings’ 6-1 start, Jefferson is off to the worst start of his career, with 28 catches for 335 yards this season. Minnesota’s offense also ranks near the bottom of the league in both points and yards per game. top.title: Tinubu has shown he cares about workers with ₦70,000 allowance — Oshiomhole
top.description: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated concern for workers’ welfare through the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance. Oshiomhole made the statement during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s performance and urged Nigerians to appreciate its policies. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” he said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, insisting that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. Oshiomhole also criticised the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which Atiku Abubakar served as vice-president, alleging that it failed to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. He said the 2027 presidential election would offer Nigerians a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whom he accused of allowing multiple exchange rates that favoured people based on their connections. The senator also faulted the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, for allegedly failing to present an alternative to Tinubu’s policies. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” Oshiomhole said. While acknowledging the right of opposition candidates to contest the presidency, he argued that Tinubu should be allowed to continue in office after “having gone through all the teething problems” rather than “recruit a new apprentice.” The post Tinubu has shown he cares about workers with ₦70,000 allowance — Oshiomhole appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: IPOB demands release of detained Igbo men, alleges persecution
top.description: ….Group says release of four men after four years in DSS custody exposes alleged injustice By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has demanded the release of Igbo people it claims are being unlawfully detained across correctional facilities in the country, alleging continued persecution of Ndigbo. The group said the recent court-ordered release of four Igbo men, who were reportedly held in the custody of the Department of State Services (DSS) for almost four years, exposed what it described as systemic injustice against the people. IPOB, in a statement by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Emma Powerful, titled, “The Persecution of Biafrans Must End: A Demand for Accountability and Rule of Law,” said the release of the four men should not be mistaken for a resolution of the wider concerns over the detention of its members. The group said its legal team had identified 83 people allegedly transferred from military custody at Wawa Barracks in Kainji, Niger State, to correctional facilities in Kuje, Keffi and Suleja. It claimed that its lawyers had communicated the names of legal representatives for the detainees to the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation. IPOB further alleged that several other people remained in detention, with some reportedly serving life sentences over cases linked to alleged membership of the group. Describing the situation as an abuse of state power, IPOB argued that political association or alleged membership of the organisation should not constitute grounds for imprisonment without proof of specific criminal offences. The group also questioned the legal basis of its proscription, arguing that the process was conducted through a civil ex parte proceeding and lacked the statutory approval required from the President under Section 2(1)(c) of the Terrorism (Prevention) Act 2013. It maintained that the signature of a Chief of Staff could not substitute for presidential approval where such approval was expressly required by law. IPOB cited the judgment in MultiChoice Nigeria Ltd v. FCCPC, involving Justice James Omotosho, to argue that statutory requirements should be applied consistently, irrespective of the parties involved. The group also referred to what it described as a subsisting inter partes ruling that IPOB was not an unlawful society, insisting that the government and prosecuting authorities should address the legal implications of the ruling. It disclosed that an appeal concerning the organisation’s status and the legality of its proscription was pending before the Supreme Court. top.title: Duke Crushes Coastal Carolina By 61
top.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 5: John Blackwell #13 of the Duke Blue Devils is fouled by Derrick Green #15 of the Coastal Carolina Chanticleers in the first half at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 5, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images C oastal Carolina came out Thursday night and quickly made it clear that this was going to be a physical game for Duke. In the first few minutes, the Chanticleers hammered Duke inside, and that continued for the whole game. Several players were in situations that could have resulted in injury. John Blackwell was thrown to the ground and grimaced in immediate pain. It looked much more serious than it was, fortunately. Ngongba got pushed backwards and hit the floor hard enough to make a noise that was heard throughout Cameron. Sebastian Wilkins got poked in the eye, which could have been quite serious. There was more, too. All it really seemed to do in the end, though, was to piss Duke off. After adjusting to what Coastal was trying to do, Duke shot out to a 16-0 lead, en route to a 113-52 win. The 61-point margin was the biggest of Jon Scheyer’s career. Pat Ngongba was particularly dominant, with a career-best 28 points. In fact, Duke and Ngongba were so dominant that he was personally outscoring Coastal Carolina until Trey Perry got the Chanticleers to 29 points with 11:33 to play. Duke’s offense was really impressive, and offense always gets the most attention, but the defense was tremendous. Coastal only shot 4-22 from deep (18 percent), and 19-63 (30 percent) overall, and a fair amount of that came after Duke eased up late. Coastal was outrebounded 53-27, and had 15 turnovers. Of those rebounds by Duke, 39 were defensive. Toss in the 17 turnovers, and that’s 56 potential shots Duke denied Coastal. Ross in 9 blocks, and that’s 65. The pressure was overwhelming, but it wasn’t just coming from defense. Duke’s offense put a lot of pressure on the Chanticleers as well. Ngongba shot 10-13/2-3, and that, alone, was almost impossible to overcome. He also had 9 rebounds. John Blackwell had 15, Dame Sarr had 12, Cayden Boozer 11, and JoJo Boumtje Boumtje had 9. Duke assisted on 25 of 38 shots, which works out to nearly 66 percent. And this is something truly impressive: Boozer had 12 assists to 1 turnover. The Blue Devils got 38 points from the bench, including 15 from Caleb Foster in just 17 minutes. Bryson Howard and Deron Rippey scored 8 each, including two breathtaking drives by Rippey. Cameron Williams got his first three-pointer, while Sebastian Wilkins scored 4, and also pulled down 11 rebounds to lead Duke in that category. Look at it this way: Ngongba, Boozer, and Wilkins each set a personal best in scoring, assists, and rebounds respectively, and Foster shot 5-7 off the bench. Consider this too: playing Coastal Carolina will probably serve them well as a warm-up for an always-physical Michigan State. Duke will see them Tuesday in Chicago. Notes – Drew Scharnow

top.title: Hardship: Northerners turn to cargo trucks for cheaper journeys despite risks
top.description: By Maryam Abdul-Aziz Usman, Damaturu POTISKUM — Despite Dangote’s ban on unauthorised passengers, Northerners still board its trucks to escape rising transport fares. In July 2026, Dangote Industries Limited offered N500,000 for credible information on illegal haulage, including unauthorised passenger transport, but travellers in Potiskum say rising fares leave them with few affordable options. Baba Iyatu, a middle-aged woman, was perched atop a Dangote compressed natural gas (CNG)-powered truck, among dozens of other passengers preparing to leave Potiskum, Yobe State. Her destination was Niger State, where her daughter had just given birth. For her, the journey was about family. But with the cost of conventional transport increasingly difficult to afford, reaching her daughter meant accepting the uncertainties of travelling on a truck designed to carry goods, not passengers. Baba Iyatu and the others knew the company prohibited unauthorised passengers on its trucks. Yet they argued that those enforcing the restrictions did not understand their economic circumstances. To them, the arrangement offered cheaper travel while giving drivers and their assistants opportunities to earn extra money. Their predicament captures a troubling reality in Nigeria: when the price of moving from one place to another becomes prohibitive, some people are willing to sacrifice comfort and safety to reach their destinations. The difference in cost is stark. Lagos fare A transport union worker known as agbero (name withheld), was interviewed at the ‘Tashan Na Tsira’ Motor Park in Potiskum, and he told the Arewa Voice correspondent that a bus journey from Potiskum to Lagos, which previously cost about N15,000, now costs approximately N35,000. By comparison, passengers can negotiate rides on heavy-duty trucks for between N5,000 and N10,000, depending on the driver’s mood. The difference can amount to as much as N30,000 on a single journey. For people already struggling with the cost of food, accommodation and other necessities, that saving can determine whether a journey is possible at all. Fuel prices have compounded the problem. In September 2026, petrol prices reached around N1,400 per litre in parts of Nigeria and N1,500 in some northern locations, while diesel exceeded N2,000 per litre, according to Reuters. Rising fuel costs add to the expenses facing transport operators, who must also contend with maintenance, spare parts and other running costs. The ruling allows the Atlantic 10 Player of the Year to return for the 2026-27 season, giving the Billikens another reason for optimism ahead of their rivalry matchup against Missouri on Friday. Joseph, popularly known as Fadojoe, expressed concern over the implications of the Federal High Court judgment concerning the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the presidential nomination of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. In a statement issued under his Operation Rescue Nigeria 2027 platform, the AA candidate said the judgment had raised questions about the independence of the judiciary, the future of political competition and the state of Nigeria’s democracy. top.title: Wisconsin stays unbeaten with tie plus shootout win at Minnesota
top.description: Top-ranked Wisconsin gave Minnesota senior goaltender Luca Di Pasquo all he could handle for 65 minutes only to take a tie out of the first matchup of the season for the border rivals Nov. 5 at 3M Arena at Mariucci in Minneapolis. For the purpose of records, the game goes down as a 1-1 tie. But after regulation and five minutes of three-on-three overtime, the Badgers’ Bruno Idžan found the net in a shootout to give the Badgers an extra point in the Big Ten standings . The game was a stark change for UW (6-0-1, 2-0-1 Big Ten) after a weekend in which it swept Notre Dame by scores of 7-1 and 9-1. Minnesota, ranked 18 th , went to 3-3-3 (1-0-2 Big Ten) with its third tie in nine games under first-year coach Brett Larson. The game was the first among three unconventional Thursday-Saturday sets the Badgers will play in the regular season. The completion scheduled for 7 p.m. Nov. 7 with streaming coverage on B1G+. UW pushed Di Pasquo to the limit Di Pasquo made 41 saves, including 16 in the second period, and four in overtime. Idžan, a sophomore from Croatia and the Badgers’ leading goal scorer, slipped a backhander around Di Pasquo on the first attempt in the shootout. On the subsequent tries, Gavin Morrissey lost the puck and Dylan Compton was denied by Di Pasquo. Wisconsin sophomore Alexis Cournoyer made 16 saves to earn his fourth win since transferring from Cornell. UW held the Golden Gophers to seven shots on goal after the first period. Wisconsin actually trailed The Badgers fell behind in a game for the first time this season when Mason Moe scored on the power play 10:19 into the opening period, resulting in the Badgers playing from behind for nearly 17 minutes. Grady Deering was in the box for the Badgers, serving a five-minute major for an illegal check to the back, a penalty that also resulted in the third-line center missing the rest of the game. Minnesota-born freshman Zach Wooten, playing on the top line with Morrissey and JJ Wiebusch, tied the game for UW with a shot from the slot 6:52 into the second period after taking a pass from Wiebusch behind the net. Wooten has scored points in five straight games with three goals and three assists. An honor for a Badger Earlier in the day, the U.S. Collegiate Selects announced that UW junior defenseman Logan Hensler, a 2025 Ottawa Senators first-round draft pick, will be a part of the team for the 2026 Spengler Cup in December in Switzerland. That means for the second straight year one of the Badgers’ top players will miss the Kwik Trip Holiday Face-off at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee, following Quinn Finley. The six-team Spengler Cup is the world’s oldest invitational hockey tournament, having started in 1923. nigeria.description: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated concern for workers’ welfare through the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance. Oshiomhole made the statement during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s performance and urged Nigerians to appreciate its policies. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” he said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. nigeria.title: Hardship: Northerners turn to cargo trucks for cheaper journeys despite risks
nigeria.description: By Maryam Abdul-Aziz Usman, Damaturu POTISKUM — Despite Dangote’s ban on unauthorised passengers, Northerners still board its trucks to escape rising transport fares. In July 2026, Dangote Industries Limited offered N500,000 for credible information on illegal haulage, including unauthorised passenger transport, but travellers in Potiskum say rising fares leave them with few affordable options. Baba Iyatu, a middle-aged woman, was perched atop a Dangote compressed natural gas (CNG)-powered truck, among dozens of other passengers preparing to leave Potiskum, Yobe State. Her destination was Niger State, where her daughter had just given birth. For her, the journey was about family. But with the cost of conventional transport increasingly difficult to afford, reaching her daughter meant accepting the uncertainties of travelling on a truck designed to carry goods, not passengers. Baba Iyatu and the others knew the company prohibited unauthorised passengers on its trucks. Yet they argued that those enforcing the restrictions did not understand their economic circumstances. To them, the arrangement offered cheaper travel while giving drivers and their assistants opportunities to earn extra money. Their predicament captures a troubling reality in Nigeria: when the price of moving from one place to another becomes prohibitive, some people are willing to sacrifice comfort and safety to reach their destinations. The difference in cost is stark. Lagos fare A transport union worker known as agbero (name withheld), was interviewed at the ‘Tashan Na Tsira’ Motor Park in Potiskum, and he told the Arewa Voice correspondent that a bus journey from Potiskum to Lagos, which previously cost about N15,000, now costs approximately N35,000. By comparison, passengers can negotiate rides on heavy-duty trucks for between N5,000 and N10,000, depending on the driver’s mood. The difference can amount to as much as N30,000 on a single journey. For people already struggling with the cost of food, accommodation and other necessities, that saving can determine whether a journey is possible at all. Fuel prices have compounded the problem. In September 2026, petrol prices reached around N1,400 per litre in parts of Nigeria and N1,500 in some northern locations, while diesel exceeded N2,000 per litre, according to Reuters. nigeria.title: 2027: Peter Obi is a trader, he hasn’t offered any alternative — Oshiomhole

Oshiomhole made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, arguing that Obi’s approach to governance was driven by short-term gains rather than long-term national development. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security, what will you do differently? He said, it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. The former Edo State governor said he respected the right of opposition candidates to contest the presidency but maintained that Tinubu deserved another term after overcoming the initial challenges of his administration. According to Oshiomhole, Nigerians should allow the President to continue rather than “recruit a new apprentice”. He also criticised the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which former Vice President Atiku Abubakar served, alleging that it failed to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke Abuja -The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, JAMB, has moved to tighten its grip on the conduct of the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination, UTME, warning that computer-based test (CBT) centres that fail to meet its prescribed standards will be denied accreditation. The Board said only centres with adequate facilities, reliable infrastructure and the operational capacity to guarantee a credible and hitch-free examination would be approved to host candidates in the 2027 exercise. JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, gave the indication during a meeting with the leadership of the Chief External Examiners, where preparations and readiness for the accreditation exercise ahead of the 2027 UTME were reviewed. According to a post on the Board’s official X handle, yesterday, the meeting was part of efforts to strengthen examination administration and ensure strict compliance with established operational standards. The Board said the accreditation exercise would serve as a critical screening mechanism to prevent inadequately equipped centres from participating in the examination, thereby protecting candidates from avoidable disruptions and compromising examination conditions. “Only centres that meet JAMB’s standards will be accredited to host the examination. For candidates, that means a fair and secure place to sit the UTME, wherever they write it,” the Board stated. nigeria.title: 2027: Peter Obi Has Not Offered Any Alternative — Oshiomhole
nigeria.description: The Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has not offered any alternative to the policies of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election. business.title: Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate Greece’s parliament approved on Thursday a bill that imposes a 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies, the first comprehensive legal framework for taxing crypto assets in the country. Cryptocurrency capital gains of up to €500 ($563) a year will be exempt from the new tax, the bill says. For bitcoin holders in Greece, that threshold is a small buffer, not a carve-out for larger positions. “Further implementation directives will be published in the coming weeks, which will also define transparency and audit rules,” a senior finance ministry official told Reuters . An earlier draft circulated in October had floated a 15% rate. The version lawmakers passed lands five points lower, while keeping the €500 annual exemption that was already in that proposal. What the levy covers for bitcoin holders The tax is set to apply from Jan. 1, 2027, Greek coverage of the finance ministry bill says. It is levied on the net gain — the difference between the acquisition price and the transfer price — not on the full sale proceeds. Trading fees and other costs tied to the deal can factor into that calculation. A taxable transfer is not limited to selling for euros. Using cryptocurrency to buy goods or services, or contributing it to cover or increase company capital, can also crystallize a gain under the new rules. That matters for anyone in Greece who pays a merchant in bitcoin rather than converting first. Simply holding bitcoin while its euro value rises does not, by itself, create a tax bill. Crypto-to-crypto swaps, such as bitcoin for another token, are treated as non-taxable events in the explanatory material that accompanied the bill, matching the approach France has used to avoid taxing every hop between coins. Net annual gains at or below €500 are exempt. Greek analyses of the text say that once net gains clear that ceiling, the 10% rate applies to the full net gain for the year, not only the slice above €500. Losses above €500 in a tax year may be carried forward for up to five years and offset only against future crypto capital gains. Purchases of crypto assets are also being pulled into Greece’s existing “source of funds” checks from 2027, so buyers may need to show that the euros used to acquire bitcoin or other tokens came from declared income or other lawful capital. The rule does not add a separate purchase tax; it widens the audit trail around how coins were funded. An EU patchwork, not a single rate European Union countries do not share a unified tax system for the sector. Rates on cryptocurrency gains typically run from about 8% to 30% across member states and are usually levied on capital gains, the finance ministry official said. Greece’s 10% sits toward the softer end of that band, below France’s often-cited 30% treatment and above Cyprus’s 8%. The same patchwork is shifting elsewhere in the bloc. entertainment.title: iDICE Named Official Deal Room Partner for Afreximbank’s CANEX WKND 2026
entertainment.description: The Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme, a US$617 million initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), will take part in Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026) as one of the event’s official Deal Room Partner. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. entertainment.title: African Philanthropy Leaders Call for Bolder, Locally Led Giving at the 2026 APF Conference in Cape Town
entertainment.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. The conference opened on Sunday evening with a reception at Cape Point Vineyards, where Executive Director Mosun Layode welcomed delegates, members and acknowledged APF Board members, including Chair Gbenga Oyebode , Wale Adeosun , and Nyimpini Mabunda . Former Board Member Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa urged guests to look past the continent’s challenges and toward its potential and to use the days ahead to turn conversations into partnerships. It was an evening of connection before two days of ideas at the Norval Foundation. Reimagining the Future Monday, 26 October, began with a call to build bridges across regions, languages, and funding silos. Mosun Layode and Gbenga Oyebode officially opened and welcomed all delegates to the conference. Dr. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka , former Vice President of South Africa, spoke of education as a sacred right of every African child and of bringing young people into decision-making. In the first keynote, Gary Lubner, Founder of the This Day Foundation, described giving away 95 percent of his wealth during his lifetime and said it was easier and more joyful than holding it for heirs. Old money thinking, he argued, is a major barrier to giving, and generosity includes time and effort as well as cash. The numbers framed the challenge. Delegates heard that Africa needs about $1.3 trillion in financing each year, while philanthropy contributes $5 billion to $6 billion. The task is to use that small pool to unlock far larger sources, such as pension funds and fixed-income assets, so money reaches businesses that create jobs. In an afternoon keynote moderated by Marlene Ogawa of Synergos, Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa , South Africa CEO of Naspers, and Gareth Ackerman, Non-Executive Director at Pick n Pay, kept things practical: back women entrepreneurs without taking equity, start with your own family and community, use local distributors, and make it easier to travel between African countries. sports.description: Ilia Topuria’s UFC return is gaining momentum with each passing day. A couple of days ago, the former two-division champion visited his native Georgia, giving fans a glimpse of his recovery. More recently, he stopped by the iconic Didgori Battle Memorial on Mount Didgori, a site that symbolizes Georgian resilience and victory. Amid all this, Dana White also provided an important update on Topuria’s status , confirming that the Spaniard is expected to be ready to return in the first quarter of 2027. With contenders like Paddy Pimblett and Arman Tsarukyan , along with reigning champion Justin Gaethje, in the mix, it will be interesting to see what’s next for “El Matador.” “He’ll be back in ’27. We’re working on that too.” @DanaWhite confirms Ilia Topuria’s return to #UFC will happen next year. https://t.co/tbRDbrnMo4 — Jim Rome (@jimrome) November 4, 2026 ALSO READ: Dana White Gives Green Light to Alexander Volkanovski vs. Justin Gaethje Lightweight Title Fight, Reveals Potential Roadblock However, Topuria recently sat down for his first exclusive interview since his loss to Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 in June 2026. In a preview clip released by ABC Diario on Thursday, fans got a glimpse of the Spaniard’s mindset after suffering the first defeat of his professional career and falling to 17-1. He said, “I’ve been in the worst situation a fighter can possibly be in. I’ve experienced the worst day of my career. What’s worse than that? Dying?” Topuria also opened up about the psychological impact of the defeat, admitting that he had spent months questioning what went wrong. “Was something off is a question I’ve had to face over the last five or six months, but one thing is clear: you either win, or you lose; and I lost. If I wake up in the morning and look in the mirror and it was like, ‘No, no, no, no, no, this is not me.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by ABC (@abc_diario) This isn’t the first time Topuria has opened up about the loss. Back in September, he took to social media to reflect on the devastating defeat in a short video essay addressed to his son, Hugo. He offered an even deeper look into his experience following his first MMA defeat. The former double champion published a lengthy nine-part piece titled “This Is Me” on his website, taking readers through his entire journey in the sport. Topuria candidly revealed that he struggled to recognize his own face when he looked in the mirror the morning after his fight with Gaethje. He also disclosed that he suffered fractures to both orbital bones, a broken septum, and a broken foot during their brutal back-and-forth encounter. Of course, Topuria was eventually forced to retire on his stool at the end of the fourth round against Gaethje at the White House. Now, with his return potentially just months away, the big question is whether “El Matador” can rediscover the confidence that made him one of the UFC’s most feared fighters.

sports.title: Duke Crushes Coastal Carolina By 61
sports.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 5: John Blackwell #13 of the Duke Blue Devils is fouled by Derrick Green #15 of the Coastal Carolina Chanticleers in the first half at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 5, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images C oastal Carolina came out Thursday night and quickly made it clear that this was going to be a physical game for Duke. In the first few minutes, the Chanticleers hammered Duke inside, and that continued for the whole game. Several players were in situations that could have resulted in injury. John Blackwell was thrown to the ground and grimaced in immediate pain. It looked much more serious than it was, fortunately. Ngongba got pushed backwards and hit the floor hard enough to make a noise that was heard throughout Cameron. Sebastian Wilkins got poked in the eye, which could have been quite serious. There was more, too. All it really seemed to do in the end, though, was to piss Duke off. After adjusting to what Coastal was trying to do, Duke shot out to a 16-0 lead, en route to a 113-52 win. The 61-point margin was the biggest of Jon Scheyer’s career. Pat Ngongba was particularly dominant, with a career-best 28 points. In fact, Duke and Ngongba were so dominant that he was personally outscoring Coastal Carolina until Trey Perry got the Chanticleers to 29 points with 11:33 to play. Duke’s offense was really impressive, and offense always gets the most attention, but the defense was tremendous. Coastal only shot 4-22 from deep (18 percent), and 19-63 (30 percent) overall, and a fair amount of that came after Duke eased up late. Coastal was outrebounded 53-27, and had 15 turnovers. Of those rebounds by Duke, 39 were defensive. Toss in the 17 turnovers, and that’s 56 potential shots Duke denied Coastal. Ross in 9 blocks, and that’s 65. The pressure was overwhelming, but it wasn’t just coming from defense. Duke’s offense put a lot of pressure on the Chanticleers as well. Ngongba shot 10-13/2-3, and that, alone, was almost impossible to overcome. He also had 9 rebounds. John Blackwell had 15, Dame Sarr had 12, Cayden Boozer 11, and JoJo Boumtje Boumtje had 9. Duke assisted on 25 of 38 shots, which works out to nearly 66 percent. And this is something truly impressive: Boozer had 12 assists to 1 turnover. The Blue Devils got 38 points from the bench, including 15 from Caleb Foster in just 17 minutes. Bryson Howard and Deron Rippey scored 8 each, including two breathtaking drives by Rippey. Cameron Williams got his first three-pointer, while Sebastian Wilkins scored 4, and also pulled down 11 rebounds to lead Duke in that category. Look at it this way: Ngongba, Boozer, and Wilkins each set a personal best in scoring, assists, and rebounds respectively, and Foster shot 5-7 off the bench. Consider this too: playing Coastal Carolina will probably serve them well as a warm-up for an always-physical Michigan State. Duke will see them Tuesday in Chicago. Notes – Drew Scharnow

Saint Louis forward Robbie Avila will return for another year of college basketball after St. Louis City Circuit Court Judge Jason Sengheiser granted him a preliminary injunction Thursday. The ruling allows the Atlantic 10 Player of the Year to return for the 2026-27 season, giving the Billikens another reason for optimism ahead of their rivalry matchup against Missouri on Friday. As part of the decision, Sengheiser also authorized Saint Louis University to carry a 16th roster spot for Avila despite its existing 15-player limit. The arrangement will remain in place until a full trial takes place, which is not expected for several months. Consequently, Avila is expected to be available for the entire season and make his 2026-27 debut versus the Tigers. The eligibility dispute stems from the NCAA’s five-for-five framework, which allows athletes five seasons of competition within a five-year period. The eligibility clock begins when a player turns 19 or graduates from high school, whichever happens first. However, the policy was not designed to cover athletes from the 2022 high school class who had already exhausted their eligibility, prompting several players across different sports to pursue legal action. The 23-year-old participated in the NBA Summer League and verbally agreed to an Exhibit 10 contract with the franchise, but never officially signed the agreement or secured a professional contract. Avila previously spent two seasons at Indiana State under Josh Schertz before following his coach to Saint Louis. He has started 132 of his 137 collegiate appearances, averaging 17.3 points per game during his junior campaign before recording 12.8 points in 2025-26. He also converted 41% of his three-point attempts while taking approximately 4.6 shots from beyond the arc per game last season. His return holds considerable value for the Billikens coming off a 29-6 campaign that included an Atlantic 10 regular-season championship. sports.title: Wisconsin stays unbeaten with tie plus shootout win at Minnesota
sports.description: Top-ranked Wisconsin gave Minnesota senior goaltender Luca Di Pasquo all he could handle for 65 minutes only to take a tie out of the first matchup of the season for the border rivals Nov. 5 at 3M Arena at Mariucci in Minneapolis. For the purpose of records, the game goes down as a 1-1 tie. But after regulation and five minutes of three-on-three overtime, the Badgers’ Bruno Idžan found the net in a shootout to give the Badgers an extra point in the Big Ten standings . The game was a stark change for UW (6-0-1, 2-0-1 Big Ten) after a weekend in which it swept Notre Dame by scores of 7-1 and 9-1. Minnesota, ranked 18 th , went to 3-3-3 (1-0-2 Big Ten) with its third tie in nine games under first-year coach Brett Larson. The game was the first among three unconventional Thursday-Saturday sets the Badgers will play in the regular season. The completion scheduled for 7 p.m. Nov. 7 with streaming coverage on B1G+. UW pushed Di Pasquo to the limit Di Pasquo made 41 saves, including 16 in the second period, and four in overtime. Idžan, a sophomore from Croatia and the Badgers’ leading goal scorer, slipped a backhander around Di Pasquo on the first attempt in the shootout. On the subsequent tries, Gavin Morrissey lost the puck and Dylan Compton was denied by Di Pasquo. Wisconsin sophomore Alexis Cournoyer made 16 saves to earn his fourth win since transferring from Cornell. UW held the Golden Gophers to seven shots on goal after the first period. Wisconsin actually trailed The Badgers fell behind in a game for the first time this season when Mason Moe scored on the power play 10:19 into the opening period, resulting in the Badgers playing from behind for nearly 17 minutes. Grady Deering was in the box for the Badgers, serving a five-minute major for an illegal check to the back, a penalty that also resulted in the third-line center missing the rest of the game. Minnesota-born freshman Zach Wooten, playing on the top line with Morrissey and JJ Wiebusch, tied the game for UW with a shot from the slot 6:52 into the second period after taking a pass from Wiebusch behind the net. Wooten has scored points in five straight games with three goals and three assists. An honor for a Badger Earlier in the day, the U.S. Collegiate Selects announced that UW junior defenseman Logan Hensler, a 2025 Ottawa Senators first-round draft pick, will be a part of the team for the 2026 Spengler Cup in December in Switzerland. That means for the second straight year one of the Badgers’ top players will miss the Kwik Trip Holiday Face-off at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee, following Quinn Finley. The six-team Spengler Cup is the world’s oldest invitational hockey tournament, having started in 1923. The Heart of a Fighter Some folks think his drive was just natural talent. I say it was pure discipline mixed with a need to be the best. He grew up poor in Madeira, sharing a room with three siblings. His father struggled with alcohol, and Ronaldo once got expelled from school for throwing a chair at a teacher. He even had heart surgery when he was just 15. That kind of background builds a tough skin. He chased perfection in a way that seemed almost scary. technology.title: Threat actor targets Indian fintechs on weekends when defenders aren’t watching
technology.description: India’s Computer Emergency Response Team has warned the nation’s financial services industry of a “significant escalation” in attacks by what it describes as an “AI-assisted financial threat actor” that has re-targeted victims after they flubbed remediation efforts. CERT-IN first detected the attacks in October and issued advisory in which it warned digital lending platforms, fintech entities, payment service providers, and wallet operators that attackers were targeting internet-facing applications, exposed APIs and privileged endpoints. If the attackers found a way in, they tried to use payment APIs to steal money. On Thursday, the CERT published an update in which it said it continues to hear of successful attacks, including from outfits that tried to remediate their systems after earlier incidents. “The same entities have been deliberately re-targeted, including after incomplete remediation and attacks have been timed to coincide with holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring windows to delay detection and response,” the CERT warned. CERT-IN has decided the attackers need a name and chose “CRAFTY FALCON.” The security org has also revealed that the crew uses AI-enhanced tools including the ARTEX pen-testing tool, the Cairn attack search engine, and the CyberStrikeAI framework – all of which have been linked to users who appear to speak Chinese . CRAFTY FALCON’s tactics see it go looking for internet-exposed environments used for testing or development, where it finds artefacts such as shared credentials, tokens, or network paths that help it move into production systems. If it gets in, the crew re-writes victims’ applications so they do things like make unauthorized API calls. Victims’ defenses assume that only legitimate apps would call those APIs, so activity conducted by the re-written apps aren’t flagged as an attack. Even if victims suspect an attack, they have a lot to cope with because CERT-IN says CRAFTY FALCON creates many “functionally identical variants refined in rapid succession; a pattern consistent with AI-generated code and iterative AI-assisted development.” The crew also quickly exploits newly discovered vulnerabilities to keep its attacks fresh. Once it gets a toehold, the criminal crew makes tiny payments of about $0.01 to test if its attacks work. If those transfers work, CRAFTY FALCON makes larger payments. When the target is a cryptocurrency exchange or virtual digital asset service provider, the crew steals wallet keys and empties cryptocurrency wallets. Vendors of observability tools will be warming up their Indian sales teams today, because CERT-IN’s advice to Indian businesses includes improving their ability to log events, monitor for anomalies in real time, and send alerts. technology.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
technology.description: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations. One connection, works every time, needs no retries There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a "*" in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored. Passwordless accounts are commonly used for accounts that use certificate-based authentication. This setting is common for certain types of accounts. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Feds warn grocers: Don't chill on cyber defenses as freezer hacking spree heats up
technology.description: If you have any industrial smart freezers, look out. The US federal government is urging owners and operators to disconnect them from the internet, apply patches, change default passwords, and take other security measures to prevent the kind of attacks that have become prevalent in Europe. “We are seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally, putting inventory and equipment at risk,” FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman said in a statement. Since mid-October, unknown miscreants have hacked thousands of remote-controlled refrigeration systems across hundreds of grocery stores in France, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Sweden. The attacks increase the temperature inside fridges to highs of 50ºC (122°F), spoiling food, and sparking fires. The Register asked the FBI if it has documented any successful or attempted attacks against refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems in America. We had not received a response to our questions at the time of publication, nor are we aware of any documented digital attacks against these systems in American supermarkets. But there are signs that stateside operators are aware of the issue. Dutch grocery giant Ahold Delhaize, which operates US supermarket chains Food Lion, Giant Food, and Stop & Shop, last month said it proactively took IT systems offline following a cyberattack that affected most of its US and European brands. Delhaize supermarkets in Europe are among those hit by the destructive freezer attacks. The Pentagon is also reportedly treating a series of freezer malfunctions that spoiled food at military bases across the US in August as a suspected cyberattack, according to Reuters, which cited four officials familiar with the matter. In a Thursday advisory, the US FBI, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Health and Human Services, and departments of Agriculture and Transportation warned organizations about the ongoing cyber threats facing operators of industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems. “The actors may exploit vulnerabilities or weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to remotely alter settings and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards,” the agencies said . Attackers exploit these flaws by bypassing authentication, injecting arbitrary code, and abusing weak configurations, according to the feds. Once criminals gain access to the systems, they can change the temperature to spoil food or temperature-controlled medications, start fires, and ultimately harm people who consume products that haven’t been stored at proper temperatures. How to stay frosty To prevent these scenarios, the government organizations urge owners and operators to “immediately” implement best practices and security protections. technology.title: AWS Kiro aims to solve identity crisis by adding another identity: bot orchestrator
technology.description: AWS Kiro, the cloud giant's AI-oriented integrated development environment, isn't the most popular code editor. That honor goes to Microsoft's Visual Studio Code, at least as measured by Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey . Kiro might rank 27th among the listed IDEs, but then it's not really an IDE anymore. Having shrugged off reports that it played a role in outages last year, Kiro now styles itself "an agentic development environment" after a brief stint as " an agentic IDE ." It's also the inheritor of Amazon Q Developer coding assistant users, who have been directed to migrate to Kiro . It's also " an AI-powered development environment that helps you build software from prototype to production." It's "available as a desktop IDE, a command-line interface, a web app, a mobile app, and a personal AI agent (Crew)." Except that Kiro Crew is also "the persistent, open source development workspace." It's more agent infrastructure – an environment – that supports Kiro Web , IDE , and CLI . To help get Kiro through its identity crisis and perhaps make it more beloved, AWS is expanding Kiro's remit still further. The cloud giant is launching Kiro Crew bots, recalling similar efforts like OpenAI dots and Grok Bot , as well as Claude Duet and Meta Muse. Bots in Kiro Crew are software agents that attempt to carry out long-running tasks. "A bot is a new way to structure and drive agentic work," a Kiro blog post explains. "Instead of working in isolated sessions, each bot is a named, long-running agent that you define and customize for a specific part of your work. It has its own memory and runs its own sessions so you stop tracking them one by one. Kiro Crew already learns from how you work. Bots change where that learning lives." There's some appealing anthropomorphism to giving each agent a name and its own tools, permissions, and memories. You're suddenly surrounded by friends. The possible downside is how that gets billed – there's potential for a lot of duplicated context if your many agents process overlapping data without some form of shared cache. Given Amazon's concerns about internal token usage and developer complaints about runaway costs in Kiro, it seems other organizations might be curious about the potential expense of keeping bot memory isolated. technology.title: The White House is apparently a popular residential proxy exit spot
technology.description: Whether through malware or other means, devices associated with the White House network appear to be serving as residential proxy exit nodes, potentially posing security risks to one of the world's most sensitive networks. News of the security snafu comes from security firm Layer3 Intel, which reported this week that it discovered the likely illicit activity thanks to its recently launched Residential Proxy Observatory . According to Layer3 founder Sergiy Usatyuk, the White House residential proxy activity might have gone unnoticed if not for the new tool. “The observatory is just a public interface to explore the data we've been collecting for the past year,” Usatyuk told The Register in an email. For those unfamiliar with residential proxies, they're like any old proxy network that obfuscates the location of a user, except in this case their exit nodes use IP addresses associated with residential internet connections, as opposed to datacenters. While many are legitimate, others are exploited by threat actors and used in the commission of cybercrimes, as the FBI warned earlier this year. The FBI bulletin, put out in March, warns users to protect their systems against hijacking via malware, illicit SDK partnerships, VPNs with hidden service terms that repurpose user computers as exit nodes, and other threats used to turn victims into nodes without their consent. Residential proxies are commonly used by threat actors to conceal command-and-control (C2) infrastructure, conduct phishing attacks, send spam, disguise malicious traffic, and the like, the FBI explained. According to Layer3, its data shows 28 distinct residential proxy services exiting into the White House network nearly every day between October 5 and November 3, with 236 separate exits in that period. Other residential proxy detection services logged the same information, Layer3 said. Most of the activity was happening in the evening, White House time, between 5 pm and midnight. That, Layer3 said, suggests someone at the White House - not a guest - has an infected device that’s serving as an exit, likely via an infected proxy SDK. If correct, that’s a problem. “Past research has shown that poorly secured proxy SDKs can allow internal network access and lateral movement,” Layer3 explained. “If an SDK on this network has the same kind of flaw, anyone buying proxy access could use it to reach internal systems.” In other words, this is a serious security risk, and one Usatyuk tells us could have been a problem for a while. “Our data retention period goes back to July 10,” the Layer3 founder explained. “Given that there was continuous activity for a matter of months and other res proxy detection services independently verified the data, it's likely that White House IPs have been used by res proxy networks for all sorts of activity for some time now.” Usatyuk said his firm’s data isn’t detailed enough to know how many machines are being used as exit nodes inside the White House network. technology.title: BMW bumps battery for the better: The 2027 i7 60 xDrive, driven
technology.description: BMW provided flights from Washington, DC, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the 2027 i7 as well as the 2027 iX5 and X5. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. When BMW debuted the new 7 Series in 2022, it set a new standard for large luxury sedans, increasingly irrelevant though that class is. Rather than siloing off an electric alternative like Mercedes, with its EQS alongside the normal S-Class, BMW simply made the powertrain an option. Stick with a V8 if you want, or consider the rather good electric version instead—only subtle differences like the badging and lack of exhaust pipes give the game away. Since then, BMW has brought out a string of even newer electric vehicles for the 5 and 3 Series (plus their SUV counterparts). It has switched from battery packs made of prismatic cells to more energy-dense arrangements of cylindrical cells. The motors are still electrically excited synchronous ones, but now the drive units feature silicon carbide inverters and more compact packaging. This sixth-generation electric powertrain was designed for the clean-sheet Neue Klasse family, which also threw out the legacy cruft of dozens and dozens of discrete single-function electronic control units for a handful of powerful domain controllers. These computers take over those functions but with much faster processing power—and therefore more capabilities in terms of chassis control or powertrain efficiency—as well as the ability to be more easily updated. science.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 6 – A… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Farewell to Swift Explanation: It is time to say goodbye to NASA ‘s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory . After nearly 22 years of service, the satellite re-entered Earth’s atmosphere on November 4 at 7:39 EST over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia . The featured image is a mosaic created in 2018 using the first one million images captured by the satellite’s Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope . Swift had a combination of instruments, including an X-ray telescope and a gamma-ray telescope , that worked together to enable humanity to study, in unprecedented detail, the fastest and most energetic explosions in the universe. The most recent solar maximum accelerated the decay of the satellite’s orbit. An innovative mission to rescue Swift by boosting its orbit was not successful . Swift burned on reentry like a shooting star, but the impressive data acquired by the telescope over its mission will continue to bring light to the mysteries of the cosmos for years to come. May it keep inspiring new missions to boldly go into space, explore new data and seek out new science. Tomorrow’s picture: what’s next? science.title: Taking a Gander at Utah’s Goosenecks
science.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Taking a Gander at Utah’s… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 6, 2026 Tens of millions of years ago, the San Juan River in what is now southern Utah shared some characteristics with today’s Mississippi River. In a bygone geologic era, the San Juan flowed across a relatively flat plain that formed in an ancient marine environment. Unencumbered by rugged terrain, the river was free to take a long, meandering path on its gradual journey downslope. But this part of the San Juan changed when geologic forces pushed the Colorado Plateau upward. Some experts think that within the later stages of this “ still-enigmatic ” history, starting around 20 million years ago, the plateau’s rise elevated the San Juan’s headwaters , which increased the river’s gradient and sped its flow. With that, the water’s erosive power intensified, and the river started carving its winding path deeper and deeper through 300-million-year-old rock. Today, on its westward path to Lake Powell, the San Juan River flows through an impressive series of entrenched meanders, also known as “goosenecks.” An astronaut aboard the International Space Station photographed the stark desert topography on October 6, 2026. In Utah’s Goosenecks State Park , the river runs through a canyon 1,000 feet (300 meters) deep. In places, it nearly loops back on itself, making horseshoe-shaped bends. One section is so curvy that the river travels 5.5 miles (8.9 kilometers) between two points that are only 1.3 miles (2.1 kilometers) apart as the crow—nay, goose—flies. Entrenched meanders in Utah’s Goosenecks State Park are bathed in golden light on August 8, 2016. Photo by Bob Wick (BLM) While the goosenecks are an unusual geologic wonder to behold by day, the area’s dark skies are a spectacle by night. Goosenecks State Park’s remote, high-desert location and 360-degree views of the sky helped earn it an International Dark Sky Park designation in 2021. According to DarkSky International, features such as the Double Cluster in Perseus and the Messier 24 star cloud in the Sagittarius spiral arm of the Milky Way are visible to the unaided eye from the park. In November 2026 , dark skies offer the chance to view several meteor showers, with the Northern Taurids, Southern Taurids, and Leonids reaching their peaks throughout the month. science.title: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
science.description: null Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT). NASA astronaut Anil Menon (at far right) is seen at the base of the newly-deployed eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) Repeating many of the same tasks as they did on an Oct. 29 spacewalk that added the penultimate iROSA, Menon and Kutryk worked this time on the starboard side of the station's backbone truss on the 3B power channel. The two retrieved the 750-pound (340 kilograms) iROSA assembly from a temporary stowage platform, carried it to the worksite by way of the Canadarm2 robotic arm and mounted it to its previously assembled bracket kit. Menon then attached the cables to tie the iROSA into the station's systems but ran into a problem. "We are seeing half of the expected shunt current that we want," radioed Nichole Stilwell, a NASA astronaut serving as the spacewalk officer in Mission Control. "In this current config, we are not necessarily going to deploy." To address the issue, the connectors needed to be inspected. Out of safety concerns — given that the arrays generate electricity whenever lit by the sun — the astronauts needed to wait for the space station to enter the shadow of Earth to see what could be done. In the interim, they spent the time cleaning up their worksite and returning the Canadarm2 to its park site as they would have done after the deployment. Fortunately, they were able to clear the issue. "We are seeing good shunt currents on the ground, so we are go for deploy," said Stilwell. Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk (at center) works on mounting the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) After releasing two bolts, Kutryk and Menon watched as the array started to unfurl to its full 63-foot (19 meters) length. No motor was needed; the iROSA, as designed, used only the potential energy stored by its rolled-up carbon composite booms to extend itself. The entire process took about 10 minutes. "Today marks the completion of not just one solar array but, over 15 years after its development, eight arrays," said Menon at the close of the spacewalk. "These solar arrays are incredible. Half the size of the old ones and bringing 40% more power." NASA graphic showing the location and power channel

science.title: Andy Weir says his new sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' is a way to 'revive the old art of radio plays' (interview)
science.description: null Hot off the tremendous theatrical success of this year's "Project Hail Mary," adapted from Andy Weir's 2021 novel of the same name, the New York Times bestselling author is rocketing back into deep space with a brand new Audible Original release landing on Nov. 5, 2026, titled " Exoplanet ." Weir (" The Martian ") is executive producing this ambitious full-cast audiobook drama with acclaimed author and ace comic writer Benjamin Percy ("Wolverine") for the first in a series of curated sci-fi projects for Amazon's Audible. The seven-episode sci-fi thriller stars the vocal talents of Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo in a wild time-travel space disaster odyssey that also benefits from Lucasfilm’s Skywalker Sound, which provided the show’s immersive acoustic elements. "One crew. One planet. Three timelines. No one survives alone," states the official synopsis. "When a quantum anomaly tears apart the starship Wild Blue Yonder, each surviving crew member crash-lands in a different era on the same deadly exoplanet—hunted, alone, and running out of time." Ahead of the audio drama's launch, we sat down with Weir and Percy to find out more about this exciting science fiction adventure. Andy Weir has already been responsible for one sci-fi hit this year, as his novel "Project Hail Mary" received a stunning movie adaptation starring Ryan Gosling. (Image credit: Getty Images (Dimitrios Kambouris)) When Percy was first approached by Audible about this challenging endeavor, it was part of a bake-off situation where he was competing with several other writers, all jockeying for position. "I think the thing that set me apart is my understanding of how to channel legacy properties," Percy tells Space. "Having written for DC and for Marvel, I can take 'Star Wars' or 'Predator' or Wolverine or Batman and honor that legacy but also put my own unique spin on it. "When it came to the banner of 'Andy Weir Presents,' my job was to write my best version of an awesome Andy Weir story. So I thought about space disasters, big-hearted hopefulness, quippy humor, and a roller coaster plot, and then I nested into all of that a time-travel story." Writing an audio drama is unlike the comic work that Percy is known for, but as he explains, it's also quite different from working on conventional shows and movies too. "If you’re watching TV or film, you’re passive and letting it wash over you. You’re taking in the story as a passenger," notes Percy. "But when you're listening to audio, you're invited in with the dialogue, the narration, the sound cues. You’re invited to fill in the vacancies.
